verdict.rationale: pnpm documents a frozen-lockfile mode that turns on automatically in CI. In that mode, installation fails when the lockfile is present but needs an update, which is the core fail-on-mismatch behavior. However, the evidence only shows this as automatic CI detection, not as a platform-engineer-controlled flag or setting that can be enforced in any environment. Missing for 10: a documented explicit frozen-lockfile flag/config for enforcement outside CI auto-detection, detail on the manifest-vs-lockfile mismatch error behavior, and independent/hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can enforce a frozen/immutable lockfile mode that fails the install when the manifest and lockfile disagree

citations.quote: When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.
In a CI environment, installation fails if a lockfile is present but needs an update.
The lockfile is left untouched, so frozen installs still validate
